_comment: IR agent span-based metrics, applied by Apply-DatadogConfig.ps1.
API: https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/spans-metrics/
create  POST  /api/v2/apm/config/metrics
read    GET   /api/v2/apm/config/metrics/{metric_id}
update  PATCH /api/v2/apm/config/metrics/{metric_id}
The metric_id IS the metric name. Create sends data.id + data.type +
data.attributes; update sends data.type + data.attributes only (no id --
it is in the URL, and the name is immutable).
PATCH IS NARROWER THAN POST. Verified against the Datadog v2 OpenAPI spec
(https://docs.datadoghq.com/resources/json/full_spec_v2.json, schema
SpansMetricUpdateAttributes): an update accepts ONLY
compute.include_percentiles, filter and group_by. aggregation_type and
compute.path are NOT updatable -- changing either means deleting the metric
and recreating it. The apply script detects that case and refuses rather
than sending a PATCH that would silently no-op.
WHY THIS UNIT EXISTS. app/app_utils/dd_run_plugin.py opens one ir.sub_agent
APM span per sub-agent and stamps that sub-agent's tokens and cost onto it.
Those are plain APM spans with no LLM Obs span_kind, so ddtrace's
LLMObsProcessor skips them and they contribute nothing to ml_obs.span*.
Making them LLM Obs spans would not help either: the only tags on ml_obs.*
metrics are env, error, ml_app, model_name, model_provider, service,
span_kind and version, so a sub-agent NAME could never reach a metric
group-by that way. Span-based metrics are the path that works -- Datadog
computes them from spans ingested by APM regardless of retention filters
(https://docs.datadoghq.com/tracing/trace_pipeline/generate_metrics/), and
each metric names its own group_by tags.
DELIBERATELY NOT PER-ENVIRONMENT. A span-based metric is org-level config
keyed by metric NAME, so a dev copy and a test copy of the same name are
two definitions fighting over one Datadog object. These carry NO env filter
and expose env as a group_by tag instead; every environment's spans feed the
same metric and each dashboard scopes with its own $env template variable.
NAMING RULE ON THE SPANS: _est means ESTIMATED, no suffix means BILLED.
iragent.{cost_usd,tokens,input_tokens,output_tokens}_est -- litellm list
price and model-reported counts. Every per-sub-agent number is one of
these; the root span carries them as the run estimate.
iragent.{cost_usd,tokens} -- root span only, Bifrost BILLED figures.
ABSENT when Bifrost could not answer, never backfilled, so these two are
safe to sum without a group_by. iragent.cost_source records which a run
produced (bifrost / estimate_only).
Never add a billed series to an estimated one: ADO-200025 measured them ~15
percent apart on cost and ~57 percent apart on tokens over identical traffic.
Cardinality is bounded: the root SequentialAgent has ~15 named children, so
sub_agent is a small tag, not an unbounded id. Note what is deliberately
NOT a group_by here: incident_id and invocation_id are unbounded, and a
custom metric is billed per distinct combination of name and tag values.
The dashboard's per-run sub-agent table reads those from the SPAN index
instead, where a tag costs nothing.
ir_agent.sub_agent.tool_calls is PROVISIONAL -- the span field it reads does
not exist yet. See its own _note below before applying it.
Tag prefix is lowercase iragent. -- Datadog normalizes span and metric tag
keys to lowercase (https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/tagging/).

metrics._note: Named _est to match the span field. litellm list price, not the invoice.

PROVISIONAL -- THE SPAN FIELD DOES NOT EXIST YET. Verified against app/app_utils/dd_run_plugin.py on branch ado-200004: the ir.sub_agent span carries iragent.{input_tokens_est,output_tokens_est,tokens_est,cost_usd_est} plus the iragent.sub_agent tag, and no tool-call counter of any kind. Another agent is adding one. This metric is written against the name iragent.tool_calls; if the shipped field name differs, fix compute.path HERE rather than substituting a different source. Do NOT derive per-sub-agent tool calls from ml_obs.span{span_kind:tool} -- that metric has no sub_agent dimension and would attribute every tool call to every sub-agent. Applying this before the field ships creates a metric that reports nothing, which is harmless; applying it against the WRONG field silently reports the wrong number, which is not.

Run-level rollup, BILLED ONLY. A run Bifrost could not price contributes NO point rather than a list-price one, so the series is safe to sum without grouping. cost_source stays a group_by so the billed/estimate_only split is visible. The root span is the only one carrying @iragent.outcome (dd_tags._ALWAYS_TAGGED), which is what separates it from the sub-agent spans.
Billed-only, like ir_agent.run.cost_usd. ir_agent.run.tokens_est is the estimated counterpart, populated on every run.
